sections.title: How To Stop Sounding Unprofessional At Work

items.q: What should you remember about **Pause is the universal filler replacement**?
items.a: **um/uh/so signal scatterbrain; silence signals confidence and clarity.**

items.q: What should you remember about **Chopin at 2× speed**?
items.a: **rushing when nervous delivers correct content in** the wrong experience; slowing down gives the brain time to think and calms the nervous system.

items.q: What should you remember about **Softeners make ideas walk in limping**?
items.a: **"Sorry, just a quick question" / "I** might be wrong but" give listeners permission to dismiss you before the idea lands.

items.q: What should you remember about **Self-obsession consumes delivery bandwidth**?
items.a: **CEO backstage fix: "It's not about you** — it's about the 2,500 people you're about to serve.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Unstructured thoughts = loose parts on the doorstep**?
items.a: **PARA turns green-screen rationale into Point** → Action → Result → Ask; listener assembles nothing in real time.

items.q: What should you remember about **Backstory overload from anxiety**?
items.a: **you front-load context because you fear** they won't understand; repeating their question back buys a beat to answer the *ask*.

items.q: What should you remember about **Interrupting = discomfort with silence**?
items.a: **2-second hold after they finish often** yields deeper sharing; "Tell me more about that" opens depth without hijacking.

items.q: What should you remember about **Main character syndrome feels like being the life of the party**?
items.a: **Dale Carnegie line**: *"The most interesting people in any room are the people most interested in everyone else."*.

items.q: What should you remember about **One vocal register = one perceived personality**?
items.a: **camera Vinh ≠ lunch Vinh ≠ kids** Vinh ≠ apologetic Peter call; authenticity is playing the full instrument, not five familiar keys.
